quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: When riding over an uneven surface, rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact force. This helps prevent the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets the wearer see far to the sides when needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets the wearer see far to the sides when needed.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet allows you to see far to the sides as needed for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels with the maker's name, instructions, and information about safety standards they meet.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, make sure you can:

options.text: See the lane behind you and the lane next to you.
See only the lane behind you.
See only the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors so you can see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. A mirror may show the edge of your arm or shoulder, but seeing the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are even more important than signals on larger vehicles.
Should only be used when another vehicle is right next to you.
Are less important than signals on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are even more important than signals on larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because motorcycle riders are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers, using signals correctly is even more important for motorcyclists.

questions.question: A motorcycle must have all of the following equipment, except:

options.text: A blue reflector on the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: A blue reflector on the rear.
questions.explanation: In Utah, motorcycles must have: one headlamp; one taillamp; a lamp to light the rear license plate with white light; one red reflector on the rear; one stop lamp; brakes; a horn or warning device; a muffler and emission system; a mirror; tires with at least 2/32 inch tread depth; footrests for passengers; handlebars; and turn signals if made after 1973.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, the effects:

options.text: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
Are less dangerous than when either is used alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can affect your riding ability. Some drugs become more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be reduced by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection against injury in an accident.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Skip wearing a jacket in warm weather.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of proper material when riding, even in warm weather. This protects you and helps prevent dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in shoelaces to prevent them from catching on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap
questions.explanation: Wear proper protective clothing when riding. Protective gear includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: When checking your motorcycle before riding, make sure:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause some friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Check each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and holds the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is true about low-speed crashes?

options.text: Happen frequently, so there is no need to worry about them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be fatal.
questions.explanation: Even at low speeds, motorcycle crashes can be fatal. Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: When should you increase the space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When conditions will make stopping more difficult than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver in front of you from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions will make stopping more difficult than usual.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle will take longer to stop than normal. Do this on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What material are motorcycle gloves usually made of?
questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: What should an approved helmet allow?

options.text: Allows the wearer to see as far to the sides as is necessary for safe riding.
Does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows the wearer to see as far to the sides as is necessary for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet will not limit your vision. You will be able to see as far as you need to for safe riding.

questions.question: What should you do with shoelaces while riding?

options.text: Should be taken off of the footwear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be tucked in.
questions.explanation: Tuck shoelaces in securely so they do not catch on your motorcycle while riding.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take and when should you do it?

options.text: A few minutes and should be done no more than once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and should be performed by a mechanic.
Over an hour and must only be done if you will be carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a thorough pre-ride inspection before every ride. It usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rider more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride more slowly, start braking sooner, keep a larger space between vehicles, and wait for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: What type of soles should motorcycle boots have?

options.text: Are made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.
Are made of soft, flimsy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.
questions.explanation: Choose riding boots or shoes that are high and sturdy with ankle support. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: How noticeable is a motorcycle brake light compared to a car's brake lights?

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
More easily seen than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing down or stopping to help other drivers notice.

questions.question: The faster you drink, what happens?

options.text: More alcohol builds up in your body.
The effects of alcohol are less serious.
You are less likely to get pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: More alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the more alcohol builds up in your body. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get ahead of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Going faster may make things more dangerous by encouraging them to follow you at the higher speed.

questions.question: What can help you avoid being in an accident?

options.text: Try to blend in with traffic and stay unnoticed.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your turn signals, brake lights, and proper lane position to show your plans. Keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready to respond to any hazards.

questions.question: What helps protect your head and neck in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to reduce head and neck injuries during a crash.

questions.question: When it is clear you are going to turn, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to use a turn signal.
You should still use a turn signal.
Use a turn signal only if pedestrians are nearby.
Use a turn signal only at a traffic light.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use turn signals when you turn or change lanes, even if you think it is obvious. Other drivers may not see you or may not have noticed you yet.
